jobs.title: Public Finance Investment Banking Director – Senior Living
jobs.description:
Job Description:

At Piper Sandler, we connect capital with opportunity to build a better future. We enable growth and success of our clients through deep sector expertise, candid advice and a differentiated, highly productive culture. Our mission is to recruit, develop, and retain high-performing people that are bright, committed, and who work in partnership with others to achieve at a high level.

About our Public Finance Group
We are a national public finance investment banking franchise with a diversified business focused on middle market issuers and specialty sector expertise. Our core business is partnering with not-for-profits, private developers, and state and local governments to raise capital for infrastructure projects through the issuance of tax-exempt and taxable bonds. We finance a broad spectrum of projects across our regional footprint and our specialty sector coverage. Learn more about our public finance team here .

We are currently looking for a Public Finance Investment Banking Director to join the public finance Senior Living team. This role can be based in any of our regional offices, offering flexibility for the right candidate regardless of location.

About the Role
The Director will serve as a senior member of the Senior Living team, responsible for leading deal origination, structuring, and execution for clients across the senior living and long-term care sector. We are interested in candidates who bring deep industry expertise, strong relationships, strategic insight, and the ability to develop new business opportunities. This individual will manage day-to-day client relationships, oversee transaction teams, and play a lead role in expanding the firm's presence within the sector. Depending on the candidate’s background, the role may emphasize sector origination, strategic planning, relationship development, and franchise building, with transaction execution responsibilities calibrated to the individual’s experience.

Key Responsibilities
- Client Relationship Management:  Build and sustain strong relationships with senior living providers, not-for-profit sponsors, and other issuers within the sector.
- Origination & Business Development:  Identify and cultivate new client relationships and strategic opportunities; engage senior living leaders in consultative discussions regarding capital needs, growth plans, affiliations, refinancing, campus repositioning, and long-term financial strategy.
- Transaction Execution:  Lead the structuring and execution of bond issuances, refinancings, and other capital markets transactions specific to senior living financings.
- Quantitative Modeling:  Develop and oversee financial models to structure and optimize debt transactions, including calculating debt service and sizing bond issues.
- Strategic Advisory:  Provide expert guidance to clients on capital raising, debt structuring, and long-term financial planning.
- Team Leadership & Mentorship:  Lead and mentor Associates and Analysts, fostering a collaborative, high-performance culture consistent with the group's mentorship-driven approach.
- Market Intelligence:  Maintain a deep understanding of trends, competitive dynamics, and regulatory developments within the senior living and long-term care space.
- Cross-Functional Collaboration:  Partner with internal teams across capital markets, credit, and public finance to deliver comprehensive client solutions.
- Recruiting & Franchise Building:  Contribute to the identification and recruitment of new talent for the group, along with other franchise-building initiatives.

Who We Are Looking For
We are open to candidates from a variety of professional backgrounds, including:
- Public finance or investment banking;
- Municipal advisory or financial advisory;
- Senior living or long-term care operations;
- Chief financial officer, finance, or development roles at nonprofit senior living organizations;
- Healthcare finance or real estate finance;
- Strategic, management, or capital-planning consulting; or
- Related roles involving senior living strategy, capital formation, debt financing, or institutional relationship development.

The strongest candidates will combine sector credibility, sound financial judgment, strong communication skills, and the ability to build trusted relationships with boards, CEOs, CFOs, developers, lenders, investors, and other sector participants.

Qualifications & Skills
- Bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics, or related discipline; MBA a plus.
- 7+ years of relevant experience in investment banking, public finance, municipal advisory, senior living, long-term care, healthcare finance, consulting, development, or a related field.
- Familiarity with senior living and long-term care operating models, capital needs, debt structures, and the financing considerations affecting nonprofit and other healthcare providers. Experience with tax-exempt bonds, taxable debt, bank financing, private placements, or municipal finance is preferred but not required for candidates with relevant industry experience.
- Proven track record of client relationship management and successful transaction execution.
- Strong financial modeling and analytical capabilities.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- Series 52 and 63 and 7 licenses required or willingness to obtain
- Demonstrated leadership experience, including managing and developing junior team members.

Piper Sandler values a strong culture dedicated to the emotional and physical well-being of our employees. Learn more about our commitment to our employees' health, well-being, our benefits program and how we are here for our employees and their families today, tomorrow and beyond here .

The anticipated starting salary range for individuals expressing interest in this position is $150,000 - $200,000 per year. Placement within this range is dependent upon level of experience, location and other factors. This position is eligible for annual incentive compensation which will be part of the total compensation. Total compensation for this position will be competitive with the market.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, creed, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, age, marital status, status as a protected veteran or status with regard to public assistance.

Piper Sandler’s Private Capital Advisory group (“PCA”) provides comprehensive, tailored solutions throughout an alternative investment manager’s lifecycle. PCA operates across three core business lines: Private Funds, Secondary Capital Advisory, and Capital Solutions.

We are currently looking for a Private Funds Distribution Associate to join the Private Funds Group (“PFG”) in Dallas.

The associate will support the placement of private-market investment funds with investors in the Midwest, Southand West Coast helping senior team members develop investor relationships and execute fundraising mandates. The associate will support the distribution of multiple fundraising mandates simultaneously, helping ensure effective communication among fund managers, investors, and internal teams. This client-facing role requires strong interpersonal and organizational skills, an interest in the alternative investment industry, and the ability to manage multiple workstreams in a fast-paced environment. The role offers exposure to investor coverage, fundraising strategy, and collaboration across PCA’s core business lines.

Key deal execution tasks include:

·       Support senior team members in maintaining and developing relationships with LPs, consultants, and other institutional and high-net-worth investors in the Midwest, South and West Coast Regions
·       Assist with the execution of fundraising mandates, including investor targeting, outreach, meeting preparation, follow-up, and process tracking
·       Develop working knowledge of GP clients, fund products, investment strategies, and target investor profiles; help communicate each client’s value proposition to prospective investors
·       Prepare and maintain investor materials, meeting notes, coverage plans, and CRM records, including timely updates to CRM
·       Coordinate investor meetings, roadshows, due diligence sessions, and follow-up processes.
·       Monitor investor allocation trends, market activity, competitors, and relevant private-markets developments; share insights with the team
·       Work collaboratively with project management and colleagues across PCA to support a coordinated client and investor experience
·       Contribute to PFG’s broader growth by identifying opportunities to deepen investor coverage and improve fundraising execution
·       Ad hoc projects and other work as assigned

Qualifications include:

- 3–5 years of relevant experience in private-fund fundraising, placement agency, institutional sales or investor coverage, private-markets investor relations, alternatives distribution, or investment banking
- Experience supporting capital-raising, investor-coverage, or other client-facing processes preferred
- Strong communication and relationship-management skills, with the ability to engage professionally with investors, clients, and colleagues
- Strong analytical skills and the ability to understand investment strategies and financial materials
- Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple fundraising workstreams and deadlines
- Proficiency in Excel and PowerPoint required; experience with DealCloud or another CRM platform preferred
- Bachelor’s degree required; a degree in finance, economics, accounting, or a related field preferred
- FINRA SIE, 7, 63 licenses or the ability to obtain them within the applicable timeframe

Our investment banking clients have access to unparalleled guidance through our deep product and sector expertise and ready access to global capital. We take pride in providing our clients with thoughtful advice and diligent execution, no matter the economic environment. Our investment banking group partners with corporate clients and financial sponsors to provide advisory and financing services related to mergers and acquisitions, equity and debt capital markets, private placements, restructuring and corporate & venture services. We offer in-depth knowledge and industry relationships in our core sectors of chemicals, consumer, diversified industrials & services, energy & power, financial services, healthcare and technology. jobs.title: Debt Capital Markets/Syndicate Vice President
jobs.description:
Job Description:

At Piper Sandler, we connect capital with opportunity to build a better future.

We believe that diverse teams with unique backgrounds, skills and experiences yield more innovative solutions. This is reflected in our commitment to engage, hire, and retain bright, committed people to work in partnership within an inclusive environment that allows each person to achieve personal success and add value to our teams and communities.

Piper Sandler is seeking a Vice President to join the Financial Services Group’s Debt Capital Markets/Syndicate team in our New York City office. This role will focus on the execution and syndication of debt capital markets transactions for financial institution clients, including banks, specialty finance companies, insurance companies, and other financial services businesses.

The Vice President will work closely with senior bankers, fixed income sales and trading professionals, issuers, investors, legal counsel, and other transaction partners to manage the marketing, pricing, allocation, and closing of debt offerings. The successful candidate will bring strong knowledge of debt capital markets, sound judgment in a fast-paced environment, and the ability to lead transaction teams while maintaining a high level of attention to detail.

This is a syndicate-focused role and differs from a traditional Debt Capital Markets coverage or advisory position. The role will emphasize transaction execution, investor engagement, market analysis, order book management, pricing strategy, allocations, and coordination across internal and external stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities
- Lead the day-to-day execution of public and private debt offerings from initial transaction preparation through pricing, allocation, closing, and post-closing activities.
- Partner with senior bankers and DCM leadership to develop transaction strategies, including structure, marketing approach, timing, pricing expectations, investor targeting, and allocation recommendations.
- Monitor market conditions, credit spreads, comparable debt securities, investor demand, and relevant macroeconomic and sector trends to inform transaction execution and pricing decisions.
- Develop and maintain detailed analyses of comparable securities, including pricing, structure, ratings, maturity, call features, size, issuer characteristics, and secondary market performance.
- Coordinate the preparation and distribution of transaction materials, including investor presentations, pricing updates, transaction summaries, order book reports, and other internal and client-facing communications.
- Organize and manage deal-related investor outreach, including roadshows, investor calls, management presentations, and other marketing activities.
- Work closely with fixed income sales and trading teams to assess investor interest, consolidate feedback, track indications of interest, and communicate updates to senior bankers and clients.
- Manage the order book and support real-time analysis of investor demand, order quality, price sensitivity, and potential execution outcomes.
- Prepare and present pricing and allocation recommendations, incorporating investor feedback, transaction objectives, market conditions, and applicable allocation guidelines.
- Coordinate allocations, confirmations, closing documentation, wire instructions, and other transaction deliverables to support an efficient and accurate closing process.
- Serve as a key point of contact for internal and external transaction participants, ensuring clear communication and timely resolution of execution issues.
- Review transaction materials and analyses prepared by Associates and Analysts for accuracy, completeness, consistency, and adherence to applicable policies and procedures.
- Lead and mentor Associates and Analysts, providing guidance on transaction execution, market analysis, investor communication, order book management, and professional development.
- Help establish and improve syndicate processes, tools, reporting, and transaction execution practices across the Financial Services Group.
- Support the development of client and investor relationships through consistent, thoughtful, and responsive engagement.
- Contribute to business development initiatives, including market updates, transaction ideas, client materials, and internal discussions regarding potential financing opportunities.
- Maintain a thorough understanding of applicable regulatory requirements, internal policies, market conventions, and best practices governing debt capital markets transactions.
- Participate in recruiting, training, and other franchise-building initiatives for the Financial Services Group.
- Perform other duties as assigned; duties, responsibilities and/or activities may change or new ones may be assigned at any time with or without notice.

Qualifications
- Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Business, Accounting, or a related field required.
- 6–10 years of relevant experience in debt capital markets, fixed income syndicate, investment banking, capital markets, or a related financial services role.
- Demonstrated experience executing debt offerings, preferably for financial institution or other financial services clients.
- Strong understanding of debt capital markets products, transaction structures, primary market execution, investor distribution, pricing, allocations, and closing processes.
- Experience working with fixed income sales and trading professionals, institutional investors, issuers, senior bankers, legal counsel, and other transaction stakeholders.
- Ability to analyze comparable debt securities and translate market data into actionable pricing, marketing, and execution recommendations.
- Demonstrated ability to manage multiple transactions and competing priorities in a time-sensitive, high-pressure environment.
- Strong leadership skills and the ability to manage deal teams, delegate effectively, review work product, and develop junior professionals.
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to communicate clearly and concisely with senior internal and external stakeholders.
- Strong judgment, problem-solving ability, and attention to detail.
- Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively across Investment Banking, Fixed Income Sales and Trading, Legal, Compliance, Operations, Accounting, and other internal teams.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and PowerPoint.
- Experience with Bloomberg, S&P Capital IQ, Intex, Dealogic, or other capital markets and financial information platforms preferred.
- FINRA licensing, including Series 7, Series 63, and Series 79 or the ability to obtain required licenses within the applicable timeframe.

Preferred Experience
- Prior experience with debt issuance and syndication for banks, insurance companies, specialty finance companies, or other financial institutions is preferred.
- Familiarity with senior unsecured debt, subordinated debt, preferred securities, regulatory capital, private placements, securitizations, or other financial services financing products.
- Experience managing live transactions and making time-sensitive recommendations regarding pricing, order book development, and allocations.
- Established relationships with institutional fixed income investors or a demonstrated understanding of investor segmentation and distribution dynamics.
- Experience leading and developing junior investment banking or capital markets professionals.

About Piper Sandler
Our investment banking clients have access to unparalleled guidance through our deep sector and product expertise and ready access to global capital. We take pride in providing our clients with thoughtful advice and diligent execution, no matter the economic environment.

Our Investment Banking Group partners with corporate clients and financial sponsors to provide advisory and financing services related to mergers and acquisitions, equity and debt capital markets, private placements, restructuring, and corporate and venture services. We offer in-depth knowledge and industry relationships across our core sectors, including financial services, healthcare, technology, consumer, services and industrials, energy and power, and chemicals.

Additionally, the team works closely with institutional investors seeking liquidity from their private assets, including LP portfolio sales. The team leverages decades of expertise in secondaries to originate, structure, and execute these transactions. The Secondary Capital Advisory group is currently seeking an experienced Analyst or Associate to support its ongoing growth.

- Facilitating due diligence and legal negotiation processes
- Interfacing directly with private equity clients, management teams, and investors
- Assisting in screening and due diligence on prospective new mandates
- Communicating regularly with Private Capital Advisory professionals and across Piper Sandler’s M&A teams
